title: Descent of lisse $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$-sheaves and their morphisms
statement:
Let $X$ be a qcqs scheme.

1. For every lisse $\QbarX$-module $L$ there are a finite $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, a lisse $E_X$-module
   $L_E$ and an isomorphism $\QbarX\otimes_{E_X}L_E\cong L$.
2. For lisse $E_X$-modules $M,N$, the map
   $\varinjlim_{F\supseteq E}\Hom_{F_X}(M_F,N_F)\to\Hom_{\QbarX}(M_{\Qlb},N_{\Qlb})$ is bijective.

Coefficient and locality conventions: fix a prime $\ell$ and an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$. Finite coefficient fields are the subextensions inside this closure [def-weil-finite-subextension-directed-set]. Work on the small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Here $E_X=p_X^*\underline E$ [def-sfb-subfield-coefficient-ring], and $\QbarX=p_X^*\underline{\Qlb}$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients], where $\underline{\Qlb}$ is the condensed ring whose continuous sections have values in a finite subextension [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed]. The inclusions are [def-sfb-subfield-coefficient-map] and [def-sfb-subfield-to-qlbar-coefficient-map]. Modules and their linear maps are the module objects of [sk-def-sfb-module-objects]. A module over a ring sheaf $A$ is lisse here if on a covering $\{V_i\to X\}$ its restrictions to the slice sites [def-pur-localized-ringed-site] are isomorphic to $(A|_{V_i})^{r_i}$ with each $r_i$ a finite nonnegative integer. Thus rank zero and varying local ranks are allowed. Scalar extension means the ordinary relative tensor product [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars]; $M_F=F_X\otimes_{E_X}M$ and $M_{\Qlb}=\QbarX\otimes_{E_X}M$, and similarly for $N$. The index in (2) is the directed poset of finite $F$ containing the given finite $E$; transition maps on Hom are scalar extension. The displayed colimit is the set of representatives $(F,\phi_F)$ modulo the equivalence generated by scalar extension to a larger field. Quasi-compact means that $X$ has a finite affine open cover, and quasi-separated has the diagonal meaning of [def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism].

proof.text: Finite trivializing covers and quasi-compact overlaps. For any finite collection of lisse modules over the same coefficient ring, take a common trivializing cover: pull back the separate covers and compose coverings, using the covering axioms of [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. By [sk-def-pe-site], Zariski open covers are pro-etale coverings. Consequently their affine members are objects of the site, and cover composition shows that refining a trivializing member by its affine open cover still gives a trivializing covering. Choose a finite affine open cover of $X$. The affine-refinement clause of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-covering], applied over each of these opens, gives finitely many affine opens $V_i$ in members of the trivializing cover whose images cover that open. The resulting finite family $\{V_i\to X\}_{i=1}^s$ is jointly surjective and still trivializes every chosen module. Since $X$ is quasi-separated and $V_i$ is quasi-compact, [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] (1) makes each $V_i\to X$ quasi-compact. For any affine open $W\subseteq X$, each inverse image in $V_i$ is therefore quasi-compact and has a finite affine open cover. The images of all these finitely many affine opens cover $W$, so the family itself satisfies the affine-refinement condition of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-covering] and is a covering. By (3) its base change to $V_j$ is quasi-compact, and (2) shows $V_i\times_XV_j$ is quasi-compact. Base-changing once more and applying (2) shows every $V_i\times_XV_j\times_XV_k$ is quasi-compact. We use this construction first for $L$, and later for $M,N$.

proof.text: Local algebra used below. On the slice over $W$, an $A$-linear map $A^a\to A^b$ is uniquely determined by the images of its $a$ standard basis sections over $W/W$. These images are $a$ columns in $A(W)^b$; naturality and linearity force its value over any $T\to W$ to be the matrix with entries restricted to $T$. Conversely this formula defines a linear sheaf map. Composition is matrix multiplication. This also treats rectangular matrices and zero ranks. The internal-module convention [sk-def-sfb-module-objects] gives the same description: an action $A\otimes_{\mathbf Z}P\to P$ is precisely a sectionwise bilinear action, by the sheafified tensor definition [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor]; its axioms and morphism equations are the usual module axioms and linearity equations. The relative tensor of [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars] is the sheafification of the sectionwise balanced tensor described in [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]: for any $B$-module sheaf $H$, maps out of the coequalizer are precisely natural $B$-linear-in-the-first-variable bilinear maps $B(T)\times P(T)\to H(T)$ satisfying $\beta(ba,x)=\beta(b,ax)$. The sectionwise tensor represents exactly these balanced maps, and sheafification preserves their maps to the sheaf $H$, so the two constructions have the identical universal property. Restriction to a slice [def-pur-localized-ringed-site] commutes with this construction: over $T/W$ the presheaf tensor is the same tensor over $A(T)$, and the coverings and all their refinement arrows are exactly the coverings and refinement arrows of $T$ in the original site. Thus the local sheafification and its identifications are the same. In particular, locally $B\otimes_A A^a\cong B^a$ via $b\otimes(x_t)_t\mapsto(bx_t)_t$, with inverse $(y_t)_t\mapsto\sum_t y_t\otimes e_t$. Scalar extension of a matrix applies $A(W)\to B(W)$ entry by entry. For $A\to B\to C$ and an $A$-module $P$, the canonical transitivity identification $C\otimes_B(B\otimes_A P)\cong C\otimes_A P$ sends $c\otimes(b\otimes x)\mapsto cb\otimes x$, with inverse $c\otimes x\mapsto c\otimes(1\otimes x)$. The balanced tensor relations make both formulas well-defined and their composites the identity, so these matrix descriptions agree under successive extensions.

source.place: Tag 03EK, section-tensor-product; elementary basis and pure-tensor calculations

proof.text: Descend the transition data of $L$. Choose the finite cover from step 1 and isomorphisms $t_i:L|_{V_i}\xrightarrow{\sim}\QbarX^{r_i}|_{V_i}$. On $V_{ij}=V_i\times_XV_j$, write $g_{ij}=t_jt_i^{-1}$ for the matrix of the change from the $i$ coordinates to the $j$ coordinates. Include every pair, also $i=j$, and include the matrix $h_{ij}$ of the inverse. There are finitely many entries altogether. By [det-lem-coefficient-finite-descent-sections] (2), applied separately to the quasi-compact $V_{ij}$, each pair's entries lie in a finite coefficient field; [def-weil-finite-subextension-directed-set] supplies a common finite field $E$ for all pairs. The coefficient changes used here are exactly the maps $E_X\to F_X$ induced by inclusions of finite extensions $E\le F$, as specified by [def-sfb-subfield-coefficient-map]; if there are no entries to descend, choose $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$. Injectivity on sections from the sections lemma implies $h_{ij}g_{ij}=I_{r_i}$ and $g_{ij}h_{ij}=I_{r_j}$ already over $E_X(V_{ij})$. On the quasi-compact triple products it likewise implies $g_{jk}g_{ij}=g_{ik}$ over $E_X$. Do not impose $g_{ii}=1$ on the whole self fibre product; only its pullback along the diagonal $V_i\to V_i\times_XV_i$ is the identity. All these equalities hold originally because the $g_{ij}$ were formed from the chosen trivializations.

source.place: Proof (1), descent of transition matrices and their inverses; corrected repeated-index convention

proof.text: Construct the finite-field model. On the slice over $V_i$ put $P_i=(E_X|_{V_i})^{r_i}$. The matrices $g_{ij}$ from step 3 define isomorphisms $P_i|_{V_{ij}}\to P_j|_{V_{ij}}$, and the triple equation is exactly the cocycle hypothesis in [lem-weil-pbc-site-module-sheaf-gluing]. Apply that theorem to $\mathcal C=X_{\mathrm{proet}}$, $U=X$, $A=E_X$, and the finite covering of step 1. It produces an $E_X$-module $L_E$ and local isomorphisms $e_i:L_E|_{V_i}\xrightarrow{\sim}P_i$ satisfying $g_{ij}e_i=e_j$ on overlaps. It is lisse by its displayed finite free local models; no global constant-rank decomposition is needed.

source.place: Tag 04TR, lemma-glue-sheaves, module version carried by the cited node

proof.text: Identify the extension with $L$. By the tensor calculations of step 2, $\QbarX\otimes_{E_X}L_E$ has local free identifications $(e_i)_{\Qlb}$ and transition matrices equal to the original $g_{ij}$. Define on $V_i$ the $\QbarX$-linear isomorphism $b_i=t_i^{-1}(e_i)_{\Qlb}$ to $L|_{V_i}$. On $V_{ij}$, $t_j^{-1}g_{ij}=t_i^{-1}$ and $(e_j)_{\Qlb}=g_{ij}(e_i)_{\Qlb}$, hence $b_j=b_i$. The morphism gluing theorem [lem-pur-sheaf-hom-cover-gluing], with ring sheaf $\QbarX$, gives a global map $b:\QbarX\otimes_{E_X}L_E\to L$. On each overlap the equality $b_i=b_j$ implies $b_i^{-1}=b_j^{-1}$, by composing on the left by $b_j^{-1}$ and on the right by $b_i^{-1}$. Thus [lem-pur-sheaf-hom-cover-gluing] also glues the local inverses to a global inverse: each composite restricts to the identity on every $V_i$, and the uniqueness clause makes that composite the global identity. Thus $b$ is an isomorphism and proves (1).

Surjectivity in (2). Take the common finite trivializing cover of $M,N$ from step 1, writing $M|_{V_i}\cong E_X^{a_i}|_{V_i}$ and $N|_{V_i}\cong E_X^{b_i}|_{V_i}$. Let $u^M_{ij},u^N_{ij}$ be their transition matrices over $E_X(V_{ij})$. A given $\QbarX$-linear map $\psi:M_{\Qlb}\to N_{\Qlb}$ is, by step 2, represented on $V_i$ by a rectangular matrix $A_i$ over $\QbarX(V_i)$. Its overlap equation is $u^N_{ij}A_i=A_j u^M_{ij}$. By [det-lem-coefficient-finite-descent-sections] (2), all entries of each $A_i$ descend to a finite field; using [def-weil-finite-subextension-directed-set], choose a common finite $F$ containing these fields and $E$. The injectivity $F_X(V_{ij})\to\QbarX(V_{ij})$ from the sections lemma implies the displayed overlap equation over $F_X$. Hence the matrices define compatible $F_X$-linear maps $M_F|_{V_i}\to N_F|_{V_i}$, which glue to $\psi_F:M_F\to N_F$ by [lem-pur-sheaf-hom-cover-gluing]. Step 2 shows its scalar extension has the matrices $A_i$, so uniqueness in the same gluing theorem gives $(\psi_F)_{\Qlb}=\psi$.

source.place: Proof (2), surjectivity, with the precise matrix overlap equation

proof.text: Injectivity in (2). Suppose representatives $\phi_F$ and $\phi_{F'}$ have the same image over $\Qlb$. Use [def-weil-finite-subextension-directed-set] to choose a finite $H$ containing $F,F'$. Step 2 identifies their extensions as two maps $M_H\to N_H$ with the same $\Qlb$-extension. On the finite common cover their difference is a matrix over $H_X(V_i)$ which becomes the zero matrix over $\QbarX(V_i)$. The injectivity in [det-lem-coefficient-finite-descent-sections] (2), since $V_i$ is quasi-compact, makes every entry zero already over $H_X(V_i)$. Uniqueness in [lem-pur-sheaf-hom-cover-gluing] then shows $(\phi_F)_H=(\phi_{F'})_H$. These representatives therefore define the same class in the colimit specified in the statement. Conversely changing representatives by scalar extension preserves the image, because the pure-tensor transitivity formula of step 2 applies entry by entry. The canonical map is thus well-defined and injective; together with step 6 it is bijective.

source.place: Proof (2), injectivity for representatives at different finite fields

split_report.summary: Completed the transition-matrix argument for both clauses using existing coefficient-section descent, module-sheaf descent and morphism-gluing nodes. Made all coefficient and locality conventions explicit; handled varying and zero ranks, finite common affine covers, quasi-compact pair/triple overlaps, inverse matrices, and Hom representatives at distinct finite fields. Corrected the false repeated-index identity in the blueprint proof; no conclusion or hypothesis changed and no new node was needed.
split_report.blueprint: Realizes Proof (1) of det-lem-coefficient-finite-descent-lisse and clause (1) of sk-thm-sfb-qlbar-two-colimit by steps 1-5; realizes Proof (2), lisse morphism descent, by steps 6-7. The same transition-matrix route is kept.

tool_uses.why: General effective descent for module sheaves on an arbitrary site supplies the gluing of finite free local models; this is the descent of sheaves invoked by the unit, not a substitute for coefficient descent.
General gluing and uniqueness of module-sheaf morphisms supplies the final local-to-global maps and equality tests; the unit has no separate morphism-gluing theorem.
Defines the sectionwise sheaf tensor used to spell out the pure-tensor calculations; it agrees with the relative coequalizer in the coefficient unit by the balanced bilinear universal property.
Only the axioms for composing and pulling back covers are used to form a common trivializing cover.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q02-e18bbe8e6 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, all 14 proof dependencies and 11 statement dependencies, the main-20261015 lemma and its proof, the unit proof and record, the meaning of lisse in sk-lem-coefficient-heart, and Stacks 0989, 04TQ and 04TR. Statement: the qcqs hypothesis and both clauses are verbatim from main-20261015. The conventions paragraph only makes explicit what the blueprint leaves implicit: E_X and QbarX as pulled-back condensed rings, module objects in Sh(X_proet,Ab) (the upstream ModuleObject category), scalar extension as the relative coequalizer, and lisse as pro-etale locally finite free with rank 0 and varying ranks allowed. Nothing is weakened. Step 1: the finite affine family is a covering by qcqs-permanence (1), since V_i is affine and X quasi-separated, together with the fpqc clause, and pair and triple overlaps are quasi-compact by (3) then (2). Step 2 (local algebra) is correctly marked elementary: it covers matrices on a slice, the comparison of internal and sectionwise modules and of the coequalizer and balanced tensor, compatibility of sheafification with slices, and a correctly typed transitivity formula. Step 3: the entries of g_ij and their inverses descend on the quasi-compact V_ij by sections node (2); composita give one E (Q_l if there are no entries); injectivity gives the inverse and cocycle identities. The source error is genuine: the blueprint's g_kk=1 fails for non-monomorphic covers. I checked the counterexample X=Spec k, V=X⊔X, where the cross component carries the matrix 2, and Stacks 04TR imposes no such identity. Steps 4 and 5: site module gluing with U=X; I checked that the local maps b_i=t_i^{-1}(e_i)_Qbar agree on overlaps, and the inverse is glued with uniqueness. Steps 6 and 7: rectangular matrices with overlap equation u^N A_i = A_j u^M descend to a common F containing E, and injectivity is proved at a compositum H. Edge cases checked: empty X, rank 0, unequal ranks on a disconnected cover, the self-overlap example. There are no new nodes and no duplicate was found. Accepted tool_uses: lem-weil-pbc-site-module-sheaf-gluing and lem-pur-sheaf-hom-cover-gluing (generic sheaf descent and morphism gluing, which the unit invokes); the other two entries are definitions. No SGA is used. No fixes.
